_comment: DEC-5 (docs/designs/gated-pipeline-master-2026-08-03.md §3) as data, per
REQ-B9/G3 (design §4). 'Review-set per change class' -- never a prose
flip (the HR-F7 rule: every flip/demotion condition lives in data a
check reads, not in a comment an operator has to remember to act on).
Consumed by adapters/claude-code/hooks/review-record-push-gate.sh's
class-gate extension (Task 18). Classes are matched against a pushed
path in ARRAY ORDER -- FIRST MATCH WINS. A path matching none of these
globs is UNCLASSIFIED and is not touched by the class-gate extension at
all (the pre-existing per-blob rrg_is_covered coverage check, if
rrg_in_surface flags the path, still applies completely unchanged --
this table is additive, never a replacement for that mechanism).
glob syntax: bash case-pattern globs (the SAME convention
review-record-gate-lib.sh's rrg_in_surface uses) -- a bare `*` already
matches across `/`, and consecutive `*` characters collapse to the same
match (POSIX fnmatch), so `**` here is written for human readability
and behaves identically to a single `*`. Matched against the
REPO-ROOT-RELATIVE path.
required_reviews[] tokens (see review-record-push-gate.sh's
_rrpg_reviewer_required_satisfied / _rrpg_harness_token_satisfied /
_rrpg_evidence_present_this_push for exactly how each token is
verified):
'harness'    -- satisfied iff the class's pushed paths all have the
PRE-EXISTING per-blob review-record-push-gate.sh
coverage (docs/reviews/records/index.json or
grandfather-manifest.json, kind=harness-change-review,
verdict=PASS). Reuses that mechanism outright -- it is
the harness reviewer's own trust root; this table
does not re-implement it.
'evidence'   -- satisfied iff THIS PUSH'S OWN commit range adds or
modifies at least one docs/plans/*evidence* artifact
(the plan Closure Contract convention already used
throughout docs/plans/).
any other token (e.g. 'architecture-reviewer', 'harness-reviewer',
'plan-fidelity-reviewer', 'code-reviewer') -- taken
as a REVIEWER AGENT TYPE: satisfied iff THIS PUSH'S
OWN commit range (the SAME added/modified-path set the
'evidence' token checks -- never the whole tree) adds
or modifies a review-record file under docs/reviews/**
(git show against local_sha, never the working tree --
same-push honoring: a record committed earlier in THIS
SAME push is visible) whose **Reviewer:** base token
(review-chain-lib.sh's rc_record_reviewer /
rc__base_token, reused verbatim) equals the token and
whose final ## Verdict:/## Delta Verdict: heading
(rc_record_verdict, reused verbatim) is PASS-shaped
(PASS | SOUND | SOUND-WITH-AMENDMENTS). SCOPING FIX
(2026-08-03, T16 plan-fidelity review F-2, Major): the
first revision of this token searched the ENTIRE tree
at local_sha, so ANY pre-existing record anywhere in
history with a matching reviewer+PASS-verdict satisfied
it FOREVER on every future push (PROVEN vacuous: the
two extant gated-pipeline design reviews already on
HEAD would have permanently satisfied the harness
class's tokens for every push from here on -- P-30's
defect relocated to push time). Scoping to the push's
OWN changed set closes that; self-test scenario CG6 is
the regression pin.
architecture_trigger_globs (harness class only): the 'if-triggered'
qualifier on the architecture-reviewer requirement -- that token is
only evaluated (and can only appear in a class's missing-reviews list)
when at least one of THIS push's harness-class paths also matches one
of these globs. Narrower than the whole harness surface on purpose:
architecture review is expensive (design §11, ~10-15 min/review) and
the design's own §11 cost model assumes it does not fire on every
harness-class push -- only on the surfaces where a wrong shape is
expensive to unwind (gate/lib/agent/config surfaces, PLUS the top-level
gate dispatchers themselves under hooks/ -- FIXED 2026-08-03, T16 F-3,
Major: the first revision's rationale claimed 'gate surfaces' but the
glob list only covered hooks/lib/**, which misses a top-level file like
hooks/review-record-push-gate.sh or hooks/dispatch-chain-gate.sh itself;
hooks/*gate*.sh closes that without widening to the WHOLE hooks/ tree,
which would over-fire on every ordinary hook edit), not on every
doc-comment or fixture edit under adapters/claude-code/**.
posture:
'exempt'            -- never checked, never logged, passes silently.
'warn'               -- missing required review(s) always WARN, never
block, regardless of flip_date (flip_date is
null for every warn-posture class below --
an operator sets one once a would-have-
blocked baseline justifies it, per M-6).
'block-after-date'   -- WARN before flip_date (calibration window,
unset/future flip_date == still calibrating,
the same convention review-chain-lib.sh's
RC_ANCHOR_CALIBRATION_END_DATE uses), BLOCK
on/after flip_date.
would-have-blocked baseline (M-6): each class row below carries its OWN
'corpus_measurement' object (T16 F-4 fix, 2026-08-03 -- the design §2/
§10 per-row machine-readable bar; the first revision deferred these
numbers to build-report prose while the harness BLOCK flip is armed,
which violates that bar). Shared methodology, stated once here rather
than repeated per row: population = non-merge commits on origin/master
in the 30 days before measured_date, path-classified via this table's
OWN globs (re-derivable: `git log origin/master --no-merges --since=
"30 days ago" --format="COMMIT_MARK %H" --raw --no-renames --no-abbrev`,
piped through the classifier). token-satisfaction methodology (HONEST
CAVEAT, load-bearing, repeated per row rather than assumed read): a
reviewer-type token is counted satisfied only when a qualifying
docs/reviews/*.md record was added/modified in THE SAME COMMIT as the
gated content -- matching the FIXED (T16 F-2) mechanism's real
semantics exactly. This is measurably STRICTER than the mechanism's
true unit of enforcement, which is a PUSH (often several commits): the
review-runner.sh workflow commits a review record under the REVIEWER'S
OWN git identity, separately from the author's content commit, and the
orchestrator pattern typically pushes both together in ONE push. Git
history retains no push-boundary data, so a precise push-grouped rate
cannot be re-derived from this repository as it stands -- the per-row
numbers below are therefore a CONSERVATIVE UPPER BOUND on the true
would-have-blocked rate (PROVEN at the same-commit granularity;
HYPOTHESIZED to overstate the true push-grouped rate -- refuted by a
future push-log-based remeasurement, not available today), not a claim
that this fraction of real historical pushes would actually have been
refused. Recorded as data for the operator's own flip-date judgment,
never auto-consumed by any code path (the HR-F7 rule: only flip_date
itself, set separately, drives behavior).

classes.baseline_note: golden: P-40 (an unreviewed harness change reaching the remote). Pre-flip_date: refused-in-warn-form -- a full {WHAT/WHY/FIX/ESCAPE} message naming the missing required review(s), printed to stderr, but the push is NOT blocked (rc unaffected by this check alone). On/after flip_date: BLOCK (rc=1) unless a fresh operator override marker covers the exact sha.

architecture_reviewer_token.denominator_note: only arch-triggered harness commits (architecture_trigger_globs match) count toward this denominator

classes.baseline_note: the pipeline never gates its own provenance artifacts (DEC-5; arch-M2's circularity concern -- a review record IS a provenance artifact, so gating docs/reviews/** on 'has this been reviewed' is self-referential by construction). Never measured; not a candidate for any future flip. NAMED WIDENING (T16 F-4 fix, Minor): DEC-5's own design text (§3) enumerates exactly four provenance surfaces -- docs/reviews/**, docs/handoffs/**, NEEDS-YOU.md, docs/backlog.md. This row adds two more, named here rather than left silent: docs/operator-todo.md joins the same operator-ledger family as NEEDS-YOU.md/docs/backlog.md (an operator-facing status/todo surface the pipeline must not self-gate, for the identical arch-M2 circularity reason); SCRATCHPAD.md is gitignored (repo root, per CLAUDE.md's 'Session working memory' section) and therefore never actually reaches a pushed commit at all -- its entry here is a documentation no-op (harmless, included for completeness against the class-table's own stated corpus rather than silently omitted) that costs nothing because the glob can never match a pushed path.

catches everything under docs/** not already claimed by provenance-docs above (array order = precedence, so provenance-docs paths never reach this arm). Own flip condition is null until a would-have-blocked baseline is measured over a calibration week of real push history (M-6) -- an operator sets flip_date here once that baseline justifies it; until then this NEVER blocks, only WARNs.
